# OpenCode v2 migration implementation plan

> **For agentic workers:** Use `executing-plans` to implement this plan in-place, task by task.

**Goal:** Replace Nix-managed OpenCode v1 with v2 while preserving Telegram, tmux status/resume, turn checkpoints, Superpowers, and Vicinae session browsing.

**Architecture:** Use the existing locked llm-agents `opencode2` package with an `opencode` launcher. Keep configuration generated by Home Manager, secrets runtime-only, and use the v2 service/client API for integrations rather than its private database schema. Port the two local plugins and retain the already dual-compatible Superpowers plugin.

**Tech stack:** Nix/Home Manager, TypeScript/JavaScript, Node.js, shell, Python source patches.

**Spec:** The compatibility audit and migration approval in this conversation.

## Global constraints

- Work in-place and preserve unrelated changes; commit the migration only when requested.
- Support aarch64-darwin, x86_64-linux, and aarch64-linux.
- Keep `opencode` as the public command used by existing scripts.
- Never embed credentials in Nix strings or the store.
- Preserve existing model/provider/MCP configuration through supported v1 normalization.

## Review focus

- Shared-server events must target the session's actual tmux pane and working directory.
- Multiple clients and Telegram-created sessions must not open duplicate windows.
- Session enumeration must paginate; migrated history and transcript types must remain readable.
- Server password/bootstrap must be available before the bot starts, including after reboot.
- Package build and config evaluation must succeed without changing unrelated inputs.

## Tasks

### 1. Package and service migration

- [x] Provide one shared `opencode` v2 package definition and use it in Home Manager and the bot service.
- [x] Upgrade the bot to v0.26.3 and refresh source/dependency hashes.
- [x] Configure v2 selection and runtime server credentials; launch one registered v2 service.
- [x] Build packages and evaluate the mac-home service configuration.

### 2. Plugins and tmux integration

- [x] Add behavioral tests for session-to-pane routing, event handling, and session directory selection.
- [x] Port agent-state/checkpoints and tmux session-opening plugins using the pinned v2 API.
- [x] Make process detection recognize the packaged executable and retain resume compatibility.
- [x] Run plugin tests and validate plugin loading in an isolated configuration.

### 3. Vicinae session integration

- [x] Replace the pinned extension's v1 SDK/database implementation with a v2 API adapter, preserving its exported interfaces.
- [x] Test history conversion, pagination, search, deletion, and request errors.
- [x] Build the patched extension and retain its Ghostty/tmux launcher patch.

### 4. Verification and deployment

- [x] Document the package, service, plugin, and session-browser architecture in AGENTS.md.
- [x] Run targeted tests and host evaluations/builds and inspect the final diff.
- [x] Apply the initial mac-home migration after authenticating sudo.
- [x] Verify installed v2 service, MCP connectivity, Superpowers, tmux opener, and bot startup.
- [ ] Apply the follow-up directory-plugin packaging fix and verify the live checkpoint plugin.

## Verification record

- OpenCode 2.0.27 and Telegram bot 0.26.3 build from the existing lockfile.
- Patched Vicinae extension and the mac-home Home Manager generation build.
- 22 regression/integration tests pass, including an actual isolated server,
  checkpoint refs, authenticated API access, shell history, and a real TUI in
  a separate tmux server.
- The built activation script initializes the credential/port before
  `setupLaunchAgents` (and declares the corresponding `reloadSystemd` ordering).
- mac-work, t480-home, yogabook-gen10 and vm-hyprland system derivations evaluate.
- Fresh-context review findings about project paths, shell transcripts,
  failed-session attention, and activation ordering were reproduced and fixed.
- Live activation requires sudo authentication; verify Telegram and provider/MCP
  connectivity after the switch. No live v1 database was migrated during testing.

## Post-activation check

After the user's `sup`, OpenCode 2.0.27 is healthy on port 49374, Telegram bot
0.26.3 reports OpenCode ready and starts successfully, all three MCP servers
connect, and Superpowers skills load. Thirteen existing terminal clients still
run the pre-upgrade binary and should be exited/reopened after their tasks finish.
An existing terminal session ID was confirmed available through the v2 API.

Live verification found that v2 silently rejects a directory server plugin whose
individual file symlinks resolve outside its root. `agent-state-v2` is now built
as a single Nix directory and linked whole. Runtime tests reproduce the failure
with the original live symlink layout, then pass against the built package via
`OPENCODE_TEST_PLUGIN_DIR`; the full 22-test suite and mac-home build pass. This
follow-up needs another `sup` because the agent cannot authenticate sudo.
